'''Rights That Hold Up in Court''' is an explainer page on [[SoapBox Law]], published at law.soapbox.community/rights. It sorts the rights that get thrown out from the rights that get you home — and shows how to tell them apart, with the actual cases.

== What it addresses ==
The page speaks directly to readers who have encountered "sovereign citizen" and pseudolegal material — the claims that a person is a "traveler" not a "driver", that a name in capital letters is a corporate "strawman", that a gold-fringed flag turns a courtroom into an admiralty ship, or that the right treaty or UCC filing confers immunity from the police.

Its stance is careful and not mocking: the '''grievances''' underneath that material are treated as real — police overreach, checkpoints far from any border, civil forfeiture, courts treating ordinary people badly. What the page rejects is the '''remedies''' being sold for those grievances, because the gap between a real grievance and a fake remedy is where people get hurt.

== Method ==
For each claim, the page gives the real legal rule and the cases that establish it, so a reader can see what actually holds up when tested — rather than what sounds empowering in a video.
